evidence: Caes. BG 7.71: quā erat nostrum opus intermissum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Our choice: the reference works have no verb for pausing a recording but Andresian’s suspendō. Classically intermittere is to break off a thing for a time (Caes., Cic.; Lewis & Short), which is what the pause button does.
Andresian’s label for the pause button. Classically to hang up (Lewis & Short), the lexicon’s hang up.

phrases.latin: Pelliculam paulisper intermitte; cēna parāta est.
phrases.english: Pause the film for a bit: dinner’s ready.

sources: Lewis & Short: intermitto · Lewis & Short: suspendo
